rounds.text: Cil Securities Ltd is deeply under-appreciated because its shares trade at a bargain price-to-book ratio of 0.56x against a book value of ₹ 66.1, with the stock sitting near the bottom of its range at just 20% of its 52-week span [E2, E5]. Valuation multiples highlight a stark discount: the company trades at a P/E of 10.21x and a P/B of 0.52x, which compare very favorably to sector benchmarks of 19.64x and 1.35x respectively [E6, E7]. Far from being a low-quality operator, the firm generates a superior return on assets of 3.49% against the sector benchmark of 1.86%, alongside an ROCE of 6.85% that beats the sector benchmark of 5.42% [E8, E10]. Operational efficiency is beginning to translate into fundamental outperformance, as recent data indicates that profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 10% [E49]. conceded: [E4, E16, E17, E62].

The bull’s reliance on low valuation multiples like P/B and P/E ignores the reality of a business in a state of terminal sales decay [E16, E17]. While the bull points to a 0.56x price-to-book ratio as a bargain [E2], this discount is justified by a persistent inability to generate meaningful shareholder returns, evidenced by a median ROE that has stagnated at 7% over the last decade and dropped to 5% in the most recent year [E26, E29, E62]. The claim of operational efficiency is contradicted by the fact that compounded sales growth has turned negative, falling to -5% over three years and -15% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on ROCE ignores that the company’s 7.0% return is barely above the sector median of 6.1%, offering little competitive advantage [E12, E68]. The lack of any dividend yield confirms that shareholders receive no tangible cash return for holding this stagnant asset [E4]. Conceded: [E6, E7, E8, E10, E49].
